title: Observability blue/green deploy strategy and stateful config rollback tooling for private installs
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: private installs have regressed during observability upgrades because stateful components (Grafana sqlite, Prometheus TSDB, alertmanager config) and Helm release ordering were updated in place. This PR implements a blue/green deployment primitive for the observability stack plus safe, idempotent state migration and a rollback plan that avoids data loss. Core changes: (1) introduce obs-blue/obs-green Helm overlay and release selector logic so the installer can provision a parallel observability stack, run migration and verification, and switch traffic by updating kube-service selectors and DNS/TCP routing; (2) add migration operators for Grafana provisioning (migrate dashboards/annotations from old DB to new, optional export/import to Postgres or PVC snapshot) and Prometheus TSDB handoff support using remote_write/receive as a fast handoff path for large instances; (3) Terraform updates to provision ephemeral routing records and a small upgrade-guard IPLB resource used during switchovers in VPC environments; (4) installer playbook additions: a step-by-step blue/green orchestration flow, automated verification (synthetic scrape jobs, rules evaluation check, core dashboards smoke tests), and explicit rollback routines that rebind services to the previous release and revert DNS. The description below is a single continuous string. Checklist: - [x] implement Helm overlay and templated release names - [x] add migration scripts and idempotent hooks - [x] add terraform resources for routing guard and optional managed-postgres - [x] add smoke tests and synthetic scrapers - [x] document runbook and rollback steps - [x] e2e smoke on k3s and constrained cluster. Impact: safer, reversible observability upgrades for private installs; minimal downtime for reads and writes; explicit path to rollback without losing dashboards or losing Prometheus samples during migration. Rollout plan: feature gated behind installer flag observability.blue_green=true; opt-in for tenants during initial release; follow-up automation to help customers schedule migrations during maintenance windows.

review_comments: Liam: Can the grafana migration be toggled per-tenant? We need to support partial migrations for multi-tenant private installs. Reply (Maya): Yes, the installer flag accepts a tenant whitelist; added example in the runbook.

Jae: Prometheus handoff is clever but I'm worried about retention windows. Suggest adding check for available disk and remap remote_write retention. Reply (Maya): added a preflight that validates disk/retention and falls back to receiver-based streaming if TSDB copy would exceed disk budget.

Anika: CI flakes on prometheus-index-tests observed in the first run — can we add retries? Reply (Maya): added a test retry hook, root cause tracked to index-lock race on small disks; added a short delay and we re-ran CI.
Liam: request for explicit DB backup step before migration. Reply (Maya): added optional PVC snapshot + s3-compatible backup task and documented it in the playbook.
Anika: approve after e2e smoke passes and docs updated. (approved)

release_notes: Adds blue/green observability deployment support and stateful migration tooling for private installs. New installer flag observability.blue_green=true enables parallel releases, automated migration and safe rollback playbooks. Includes terraform resources for ephemeral routing and optional managed-postgres provisioning. Intended to reduce risk of dashboard/data loss during obs upgrades.
